title: Emerald Tablet
ask_addressed: What does the historiography say (Newman and Principe on 'chymistry', Principe's work) about whether alchemy and chemistry were separate? And what do sceptics say about popular claims that modern chemistry is simply 'Egyptian science', or that Hermes Trismegistus / the Emerald Tablet are pharaonic-era?
quote: It is believed to have been compiled in Arabic in the late eighth or early ninth century.
summary: Earliest known text of the Tabula Smaragdina is Arabic, an appendix to the Book of the Secret of Creation; proposed dates run c. 750-833 CE. Bears against a pharaonic origin.

title: Jabir ibn Hayyan
ask_addressed: How did Greco-Egyptian alchemy reach modern chemistry: Byzantine collections, Arabic translation and Jabirian / Rhazes work, Latin translations (e.g. Robert of Chester 1144), medieval and early-modern European alchemy, Boyle, Newton, Lavoisier? quote: Jabir's name was used as a pseudonym by one or more anonymous Shi'ite alchemists
summary: Reports Kraus's c. 850-950 dating of the Jabirian corpus and Nomanul Haq's 1994 criticism of Kraus's dating and size estimate; the corpus is pseudonymous, not an eighth-century single-author work.
